newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-COLLINS EVER MORE INFLUENTIAL AT MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLLINS EVER MORE INFLUENTIAL AT MONACO.

text.p: John Collins' telling performance and winning goal in Monaco's table topping 1-0 win at Montpellier marked the Scotland midfielder's growing influence in Jean Tigana's side.

Monaco lorded it at the top of the French first division table on Friday -- at least until Paris St Germain's evening visit to Caen -- after Collins, running the midfield in the absence of suspended playmaker Ali Benarbia, stole the show on Thursday night.
The team from the principality went two points clear of PSG who had led without interruption since September.

Collins was in the box to sidefoot into the net a low cross from Nigerian Victor Ikpeba in the 51st minute, and a minute later found himself at the other end clearing a header by Montpellier's Ibrahim Bakayoko off the Monaco line.

"We all worked together and that's what's vital," said the former Glasgow Celtic player. "We mustn't forget that we were handicapped by the absence of several players. In these conditions, it's a super result that we got at Montpellier.
"I hope Paris (PSG) are upset at Caen so we can (remain) leaders of the championship for the first time this season."
It was Collins' third league goal for Monaco. He also scored in the 4-2 demolition of Borussia Moenchengladbach in the second round of the UEFA Cup.
Monaco travel to Hamburg on Tuesday for the second leg of their third round tie with a 3-0 advantage after the home leg.
